name: Home systems research for Washington County and Cedar City, Utah
description: Published facts about water chemistry, ground conditions, climate, municipal rules, homeowner associations and conservation rebates in the towns this company works in, each carrying the documents it was taken from. Compiled by St. George Home Services.
licenseNote: Use it, including commercially, with attribution to St. George Home Services. We would rather be quoted accurately than not quoted.

notes.docs_are_section_level: The `docs` on a fact are every verified document cited by the research section that fact came from. A corpus section usually cites several, so a listed document is not a promise that this specific sentence appears in it. Treat `docs` as the reading list behind the claim.
notes.withheld: Facts that did not survive checking are flagged in the source data and are not in this file. Figures are never estimated to fill a gap.
notes.verification: Every document URL was followed on its verifiedOn date. Candidates that returned 403, 404 or sat on a domain impersonating a government address were excluded rather than published.
notes.not_covered: No prices for work, no response or arrival times, and no credential beyond the Utah DOPL license named in `publisher`. See https://stgeorgehomeservices.com/llms.txt for the full list of what this company does not claim.

facts.fact: The City of St. George's Water Distribution Division instructs residents to set water softeners to 18 grains per gallon, with a maximum of 22 grains.
facts.quote: The City of St. George instructs residents to set water softeners to 18 grains per gallon, with a maximum of 22 grains.
facts.research: 05-environment-water-geology-corpus.md §1.1 The single most important number: hardness

facts.fact: 18 grains per gallon is about 308 mg/L as calcium carbonate and 22 gpg about 376 mg/L, both classed as very hard on the USGS scale.
facts.quote: 18 gpg ≈ 308 mg/L as CaCO₃; 22 gpg ≈ 376 mg/L. Both are "very hard" under the USGS scale (>180 mg/L).

facts.fact: The city asks residents to keep softener settings low because softener salt raises the dissolved-solids level of the reclaimed water the city reuses for irrigation.
facts.quote: the city asks residents to keep the setting low because softener salt raises TDS in the reclaimed irrigation water

facts.fact: St. George's 2024 water quality report shows total dissolved solids ranging from 118 to 936 ppm, and the 2025 report gives a 580 ppm average.
facts.quote: Total Dissolved Solids | 118 – 936 ppm | 580 ppm

facts.fact: Sulfate in St. George water ranges from 1.38 to 451 ppm, with a reported average of 185 ppm.
facts.quote: Sulfate | 1.38 – 451 ppm | 185 ppm

facts.fact: Calcium in St. George water ranges from 18 to 95 ppm and sodium from 5 to 153 ppm.
facts.quote: Calcium (ppm) | 18–95 ... Sodium (ppm) | 5–153

facts.fact: Arsenic in St. George water has been measured at 1 to 13 ppb with a running annual average of 8.68 to 9 ppb, against a federal limit of 10 ppb.
facts.quote: St. George's running annual average is 8.68–9 ppb against a 10 ppb MCL — the system operates close to the limit, with individual samples up to 13 ppb.

facts.fact: St. George disinfects with chlorine (residual 0.10 to 1.19 ppm), not chloramine.
facts.quote: Disinfectant is chlorine, not chloramine, in St. George and Ivins (the two systems that report it).

facts.fact: Total trihalomethanes in St. George water ranged from 0.58 to 56.6 ppb and HAA5 from not detected to 16.5 ppb; the federal TTHM limit is 80 ppb.
facts.quote: TTHM (ppb) | 0.58–56.6 ... TTHM at 35.4 ppb is below the 80 ppb MCL

facts.fact: Hexavalent chromium has been measured in St. George water at 0.279 ppb; there is no federal limit for chromium-6.
facts.quote: Chromium-6 is present and measured in St. George (0.279 ppb) and Hurricane (1.22 ppb). There is no federal MCL for chromium-6.

facts.fact: St. George water is in compliance with federal drinking-water law; arsenic at 9.58 ppb is under the 10 ppb limit and TTHM at 35.4 ppb is under the 80 ppb limit.
facts.quote: all of these systems are in compliance with federal law. Arsenic at 9.58 ppb is below the 10 ppb MCL; TTHM at 35.4 ppb is below the 80 ppb MCL.

facts.fact: No St. George water quality report publishes hardness, because hardness is not a federally required reporting parameter.
facts.quote: Hardness, pH, chloride, and iron are absent from all of them — they are not federally required reporting parameters.
facts.research: 05-environment-water-geology-corpus.md §1.1 [GAP] No Washington County CCR publishes hardness

facts.fact: Every major tankless water heater manufacturer publishes a hardness limit of 7 to 12 grains per gallon, and St. George's city-recommended 18 gpg setting exceeds all of them.
facts.quote: Every major tankless manufacturer publishes a hardness limit, and St. George's water exceeds every one of them — several by a factor of two to three.

facts.fact: Noritz's tankless warranty excludes damage from hardness above 12 grains per gallon (200 mg/L), and Rinnai, Rheem and Navien all cap total hardness at 200 mg/L. A.O. Smith's current gas tankless warranty publishes no hardness figure at all.
facts.quote: Damage as a result of use with non-potable water, untreated or poorly treated well water, or water with high PH levels or hardness levels in excess of 12 grains per gallon (200 mg/L).
facts.research: Manufacturer warranty documents, each from the maker's own site, re-verified September 2, 2026

facts.fact: Rinnai and Rheem tankless units cap total dissolved solids at 500 mg/L, and the high end of St. George's 118 to 936 ppm range exceeds that limit.
facts.quote: Rinnai and Rheem both cap TDS at 500 mg/L. St. George runs 118–936 ppm depending on source blend.

facts.fact: Softened water leaving a properly set softener is functionally 0 to 1 grain per gallon; the city's 18 gpg figure is the incoming hardness the softener is set to, not the output.
facts.quote: The city's 18 gpg is what you tell the softener the incoming water is. Softened output is functionally 0–1 gpg, which clears every limit in the table.
facts.research: 03-content-briefs.html §0.1 Write this honestly or it backfires

facts.fact: The city asks residents to avoid irrigating between 4 and 6 a.m. because simultaneous demand in that window causes a noticeable pressure drop across the distribution system.
facts.quote: A large demand for water in a short period of time creates a noticeable pressure drop in the water distribution system.

facts.fact: A water softener does not remove arsenic.
facts.quote: A water softener | Nothing. Cation exchange does not remove arsenic.

facts.fact: St. George City Code § 10-7-7 caps residential lawn at 8 percent of lot size, to a maximum of 1,500 square feet, on lots up to 20,000 square feet.
facts.quote: The total lawn area for any residential lot ... shall not exceed eight percent (8%) of the total lot size up to a maximum of one thousand five hundred (1,500) square feet for lots up to twenty thousand (20,000) square feet.

facts.research: St. George City Code § 10-7-7 (Title 10 Ch. 7, Residential Zones), retrieved September 2, 2026

facts.research: St. George City Code § 10-7-7 (Title 10 Ch. 7, Residential Zones), retrieved September 2, 2026

facts.research: St. George City Code § 10-7-7 (Title 10 Ch. 7, Residential Zones), retrieved September 2, 2026

facts.quote: Decorative water features limited to one, ≤50 gallons, with recirculating pump
facts.research: St. George City Code § 10-7-7 (Title 10 Ch. 7, Residential Zones), retrieved September 2, 2026

Minimum landscaping standards are required for development within all zones except agriculture, gravel and grazing, open space, and single-family residential
facts.research: St. George City Code § 10-23-1, retrieved September 2, 2026

facts.fact: St. George requires an approved backflow assembly on all outside watering systems, tested annually, plus hose bib vacuum breakers on every exterior hose connection.
facts.quote: It is important to install and maintain an approved Backflow Assembly on all outside watering systems ... have it tested annually.

facts.quote: St. George requires backflow assemblies on all outside watering systems — so a large share of local homes are closed systems by ordinance.

facts.quote: § 8-4-14 — traps cleaned no less than weekly; interceptors at 25% of design hydraulic depth

facts.quote: Program authority: EPA-approved June 6, 1991; enforces 40 CFR 403.5; codified at Title 8, Chapter 4.

facts.quote: St. George uses CityInspect for building permits, not CitizenServe. CitizenServe handles business licensing only.

facts.quote: Front fence height | 4 ft legal

facts.quote: All outdoor lighting shall conform to the requirements of this chapter, excluding lighting for detached single-family dwellings.

facts.fact: St. George publishes its structural design criteria as Seismic Design Category D, 105 mph wind, 21 psf ground snow, 20 psf roof snow, a 12-inch frost line and moderate-to-heavy termite exposure.
facts.quote: Seismic Design Category D, along with ground snow load 21 psf, roof snow 20 psf, wind 105 mph, frost line depth 12 inches, and moderate-to-heavy termite

facts.fact: Utah replaces the model water heater anchoring section with its own under Utah Code 15A-3-205, and Utah's version has no seismic design category trigger: anchoring or strapping is required statewide, at points within the upper third and the lower third of the appliance.
facts.quote: anchored or strapped to resist horizontal displacement ... within the upper one-third and lower one-third of the appliance's vertical dimensions

facts.fact: Utah adopts construction code statewide under Title 15A; St. George City Code §9-1-1 adopts whatever the state adopts, so the plumbing code does not vary city to city.
facts.quote: Utah adopts construction code statewide under Title 15A, so the plumbing code does not vary city to city.

facts.fact: Under WCWCD's Water Efficiency Standards, where a city ordinance and the District standard conflict, the rule giving the greater water-conservation benefit applies, so St. George's 1,500 square foot lawn cap and 15 percent slope limit govern over the District's 2,500 square foot and 25 percent figures.
facts.quote: Where these standards conflict with a municipal ordinance or the requirements of a common interest community, the regulation providing the greatest water conservation benefit shall apply.

facts.fact: WCWCD's Water Efficiency Standards (October 2023) require every drip zone to have a pressure regulator, filter, flush-end assembly and emitters rated 20 gallons per hour or less, and prohibit drip and spray on the same valve.
facts.quote: All other plant material must be irrigated from a drip irrigation system equipped with a pressure regulator, filter, flush-end assembly and emitters rated for 20 gallons per hour (gph) or less.

facts.fact: WCWCD standards require a WaterSense-labeled smart controller on automated irrigation systems, cap ornamental water features at 25 square feet per parcel, and require hot-water recirculation in homes over 1,400 square feet unless hot water arrives within 0.6 gallons.
facts.quote: Hot water recirculation required in single/multi-family over 1,400 sq ft unless hot water delivers within 0.6 gallons.

facts.fact: Under Utah Code §57-8a-231, an HOA may not require lawn in any area less than eight feet wide, which matches the city's own park-strip prohibition, so an HOA in St. George cannot lawfully require more lawn than the city permits.
facts.quote: So an HOA in St. George or Washington City cannot lawfully require more lawn than the city permits.

facts.fact: St. George's residential landscape standards apply to new construction and to a remodel that increases the dwelling's footprint, while the completion and maintenance obligations apply to all residential properties.
facts.quote: shall apply to all new development, and to the remodeling of existing dwelling units when a dwelling unit's footprint increases ... Completion and maintenance of landscaping shall apply to all residential properties.

facts.quote: springs on Pine Valley Mountain, wells in the Gunlock and Snow Canyon areas (23 wells total), and Virgin River surface water stored in Quail Creek and Sand Hollow Reservoirs

facts.quote: 850+ miles of pipe, 22 storage tanks, 16 booster pump stations, and 15,000+ valves, delivering ~50 MGD at summer peak.

facts.fact: More than 80 percent of the drinking water the Washington County Water Conservancy District delivers is Virgin River surface water; the rest is groundwater from the Navajo aquifer.
facts.quote: more than 80% of district-delivered drinking water is surface water diverted from the Virgin River
